Wall Street economists had forecast overall spending on construction to rise 0.5 percent in May.
Department officials said the 1.8 percent drop in May construction spending was the sharpest monthly decline in more than three years, since a 3.0 percent decrease in January 1994.
The 5.9 percent plunge in May public construction spending similarly was the steepest for any month since January 1994 when it fell 6.1 percent, the department said.
The department revised construction spending figures from the first of the year, resulting in substantial changes to the dollar totals in several months.
For example, in January it now says spending was at an annual rate of $577.1 billion instead of the $588.9 billion that it reported a month ago.
